cohort: This abstract is a review and does not have its own specific cohort, but it discusses findings from studies involving low birth weight, premature, preterm, and full-term babies, as well as mother-baby dyads.
finding: Kangaroo Mother Care and skin-to-skin contact offer significant health benefits for neonates, including reduced morbidity and mortality and improved breastfeeding, yet their implementation in high-income settings remains low due to factors like routine separation and medical interventions.
mod_finding: Maternal caesarean section is highlighted as an obstetric intervention that can result in separation of the mother-baby dyad, thereby contributing to the low implementation of KMC.
country: Global (with specific reference to implementation challenges in high-income settings and the UK).
followup_time: Up to six months postpartum (mentioned in the context of reviewed breastfeeding exclusivity studies).
birth_weight: Low birth weight, premature, preterm, and full-term babies were included in the studies reviewed.
gest_age: Preterm and full-term babies were included in the studies reviewed.
